ai.title: System prompt editfile block guidance update
ai.summary: System prompt guidance in backend/src/system-prompt.ts now explicitly discourages placeholder comments like `// ... rest of the file ...` in overwrite edits and emphasizes SEARCH/REPLACE blocks as the preferred format for most changes. This clarifies the expected mechanism for file edits to prevent truncation and ensure precise diff application. The change affects the internal system prompt used by the backend agent.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to edit a file, it now has clearer rules about how to do it. The guidance tells the assistant to write out complete file contents when creating or fully replacing a file, and to avoid using placeholder comments like "//... rest of the file..." to skip sections. Instead, the assistant is now encouraged to use search-and-replace style blocks to make targeted edits to parts of a file. These instructions are baked into the assistant's internal system prompt, so the change affects how the assistant approaches file editing automatically.

ai.title: Detect lazy edits in file blocks
ai.summary: Added hasLazyEdit helper to detect ellipsis-based placeholder comments in generated code. processFileBlock now checks for these patterns and triggers full file rewrite via applyRemainingChanges when detected. The rewrite prompt instructs the model to ignore lazy edit comments and preserve original content. This prevents incomplete file writes when models output placeholder comments instead of full code.

eli5.text: You may have noticed the assistant sometimes wrote placeholder comments like '// rest of the file...' instead of the full code in a response. The assistant now checks for these lazy placeholders and, when found, regenerates the complete file content to ensure you actually get the full code you need. This fix is active today for all code-writing responses.

ai.title: Simplify git staging condition in CLI
ai.summary: The condition for staging previous changes in npm-app/src/cli.ts was simplified. It now checks only `this.git === 'stage'` and `allChanges.length > 0`, removing redundant checks for `lastChanges` and `changes` lengths. This internal refactor streamlines the logic without altering user-visible behavior.

eli5.text: When you tell the assistant to stage your changes for a git commit, it now decides whether there's anything to save by looking at a single combined list of all changes, instead of checking several separate lists. You won't see any difference: the same files still get staged when the flag is on. The code just got tidier behind the scenes, making it a little easier for developers to maintain without changing what happens when you use it.

ai.title: Make node-pty optional with childprocess fallback
ai.summary: Moved @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch to optionalDependencies in npm-app/package.json. Implemented try/catch require in npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts to detect PTY availability. Added fallback logic in createPty to use child_process when node-pty fails to load. Updated npm-app/knowledge.md to document native dependency handling and fallback behavior.

eli5.text: The assistant's terminal feature now works even when a special component that makes terminal output look exactly like a real computer terminal cannot be installed. Previously, if that component failed to load, the terminal feature might not work at all; now it automatically falls back to a simpler method that still runs commands and shows output, just without the fancy text formatting. You would only notice this if you were in a situation where the terminal looked broken before, instead, it now runs commands normally. This change is live today and applies to anyone using the assistant's terminal functionality.

ai.title: Add cmd prompt regex to terminal command handler
ai.summary:
Added simpleWindowsPromptRegex3 to handleRunTerminalCommand to match bare Windows command prompt paths like "C:\...>". The new regex /[A-Z]:\
S+>/ complements existing patterns for PowerShell and time-based prompts. Updates npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts and documents Windows path regex escaping in npm-app/knowledge.md.

eli5.text: If you work with Windows command-line tools in a terminal, the assistant now recognizes an additional style of command prompt that looks like a file path followed by a greater-than sign, such as "C:\Projects>MyCommand". This means the assistant can better tell that it's looking at a Windows command prompt rather than a PowerShell or Linux-style prompt, so it handles the output correctly. The change only affects how prompts are matched internally; you won't see a menu option or setting for it.

ai.title: Version bump 1.0.133
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.133 in npm-app/package.json. Routine release increment. No functional changes.

eli5.text: If you updated to this version, you'd see the Upgrade button now appears for people who aren't logged in when they visit the pricing page, and the free plan sign-up button now correctly handles people who haven't signed in yet. Behind the scenes, the system also got better at spotting placeholder code in generated files and uses a backup method for terminal operations so it works even if the preferred tool isn't available, these are all part of the same release package.
